effects.journal: Three missed calls from her girlfriend she never answered. One outgoing call, 47 seconds, to someone saved only as J.

lines: Three missed calls from MARA ❤ between 11:49 and 12:20. She never picked up.
One outgoing call at 11:41 PM. Forty-seven seconds. To a contact saved only as "J."
Six minutes before your message. Six minutes before "keep the".

m_mara1.text: Hi. Is this {player}? This is Mara Ellison. Wren and I are together.

m_mara2.text: I found your number in her messages. I'm sorry to write so late. I don't sleep.

m_mara3.text: Have you heard from her? Anything at all. Please.

options.text: Nothing since the night she went quiet. I'd asked her to come over. I left the door open for her.

effects.journal: I told Mara the truth about the door.

options.text: No, sorry. We only talked a few times.
What are the police saying? Have they told you anything?

m_mara_truth.text: Thank you for telling me that. She talked about you. She said you were the first person here who didn't already know everything about her.

m_mara_lie.text: A few times. Right. She had your name saved with a heart, {player}. But all right.

m_mara_deflect.text: They say she's an adult and adults leave. That's the phrase. Adults leave.

m_mara_police.text: Ardis is pushing them for me. Councilwoman Locke. She got me the records job. She's been very kind.

m_mara_end.text: If she contacts you - anyone contacts you - tell me first. Before the police. Please.

g_board.text: It's official now. Open the Case Board - her photo is already pinned.

effects.journal: Started a board. One photo in the centre. Hers.

lines: A board. One pin. Her.
Around it: a locker number, a siren that should not have been on, a car that was not Jonah's truck.
It does not feel like a game. It feels like a promise.
Her messages are trying to come through. The link stops at a lock screen - hers, not yours.
Four digits. You knew her three weeks. You know exactly two numbers about her.

lines: Six messages. No replies. Not one.
A man who keeps turning up at the diner and never writes anything down.
"You were right about the number." Locker 14.

a1.text: Hello {player}. This is Ardis Locke. I'm so sorry to write so late. I saw your light on when I drove past.

a2.text: Mara told me you two were close. Has anyone told you whether they've found her phone? This town looks after its own.

options.text: I don't know. Why would that matter?
I'd assume they'd have said so.

a_reply_why.text: Only that a phone tells you where someone was. Forgive me - I'm trying to help and it comes out as questions.

a_reply_neutral.text: One would hope. Forgive me - I'm trying to help and it comes out as questions.

a_reply_cold.text: No reason at all. Forgive me. Mara said you were close to her, that's all.

a_end.text: Save my number. Day or night. Whatever you need, you call me.

notes.title: why is she recording her calls?
notes.body: Her phone kept a recording of the 47-second call. A call recorder - for her interviews, for the project. She was recording everyone who would talk about 2006. The Hollowmere files.

g_vm.text: Her phone recorded the 47-second call. Listen to it.

mg_audio.title: Recording · 47 seconds

config.brief: Play through the recording. Mark each sound behind her voice. The sounds tell you where she was.

hints: The siren is already on at the start. It does not wait.
There is a single metal strike at about thirty-one seconds. It is not the orchard.
Near the very end, before the line cuts: a heavy door.

effects.journal: Siren already on. Bell at 0:31. Car door at 0:44. The Authority says there are no night releases.

lines: "I found the box. It's exactly where he said."
Who is he? What box?
The siren is already sounding when she calls. The Authority's own website says it never sounds at night.
Thirty-one seconds: a bell. Forty-four: a car door. Then nothing.

ghost.text: i think he knows i saw it

lines: For one second, a message from Wren. Present tense.
Then, for four seconds: Wren is typing…
Then nothing.

effects.journal: A message from Wren appeared and vanished: "i think he knows i saw it." Hold vanishing messages to keep them.

Outside your window, standing in the rain, is a figure.
They take a photo of you. The flash blinds you for a second.
Your phone buzzes.
